sections.title: Your point of view
sections.description: Select walking, cycling, or both. Questions will adapt to your selection.

questions.text: How do you move through this place? You can choose both answers.

options.text: Person walking or rolling (also with a stroller, cane, walker or wheelchair)
Person cycling or riding an e-scooter

questions.text: Which of these situations apply to your trip today?

options.text: Going to or from a bus, tram or metro stop
Going to or from a parked car
Going to or from bicycle parking
Accompanying a child (for example to school)
Using a wheelchair, walker, cane or other mobility aid

questions.text: How often do you go along this street segment?

options.text: I avoid it or have stopped using it

sections.title: Quick assessment
sections.description: Answer these first. Then you can finish or add optional details.

questions.text: Is there a place for people to walk along this street?

options.text: No walking space: people walk among the cars
Only an edge of the road, without a sidewalk
Sidewalk, but it stops or is only on one side
Walking space marked on the ground, at the same level as the road
Path shared by people walking and cycling
Stairway or path with steps (stairways are assessed here)

questions.text: Is there a space for cycling on this street?
questions.help: A school street is a street next to a school that is closed to motor traffic when children arrive and leave.

options.text: No space for bicycles: people cycle in ordinary traffic
No space for bicycles, but the limit is 30 km/h or it is a school street
Cycle lane or path, but it stops
Path shared by people walking and cycling

questions.text: Which best describes using this street segment while walking?

options.text: I can pass without slowing down
I need to slow down a little
I need to be careful while passing
It takes a lot of effort or attention
I avoid using it if possible
I cannot get through (for example with a wheelchair or stroller)

questions.text: Because of traffic (cars, motorcycles, bicycles), how risky does it feel to use this street segment on foot?
Which best describes using this street segment by bicycle or e-scooter?

options.text: I can pass without slowing down
I need to slow down a little
I need to be careful while passing
It takes a lot of effort or attention
I avoid using it if possible
I cannot get through by bicycle or e-scooter

questions.text: Because of traffic, how risky does it feel to use this street segment by bicycle or e-scooter?
How safe from harassment or assault do you feel here, also in the evening?
questions.help: Harassment means unwanted comments, gestures or contact. This question is about your own feeling, not about traffic.

options.text: I do not go there in the evening

questions.text: Would you like to add more details? There are about 10 to 20 optional questions for one way of moving, and up to about 30 if you chose both (about 4–10 minutes).

sections.title: Walking space
sections.description: Look at the place. Answer only what you can see.

questions.text: How wide is the space for walking?

options.text: Only one person can just about pass
One person can pass, but not a stroller or wheelchair
A stroller or wheelchair can pass, but people cannot pass each other
Two people can pass each other
Very wide, with plenty of room to move

questions.text: If there is a raised sidewalk, how is it protected from traffic?
questions.help: Bollards are short posts that stop vehicles from entering the walking area.

options.text: Parked cars between the sidewalk and the road

questions.text: If the walking area is at road level, how is it separated from traffic?
questions.help: Bollards are short posts that stop vehicles from entering the walking area.

questions.text: Which accessibility features are available?
questions.help: Tactile paving is a ridged or dotted ground surface that blind or visually impaired people can feel with a cane or their feet.

options.text: Tactile paving for blind or visually impaired people

questions.text: Are there steps or stairs along this path?
How many steps are there?

options.text: A few steps, up to about 10

questions.text: For stairs, what helps people use them?
questions.help: A bike rail or channel is a groove at the side of the steps for pushing a bicycle.

questions.text: What problems do the stairs have?

options.text: Closed by a gate or at certain hours

sections.title: Cycling space
sections.description: Look at the place. Answer only what you can see.

questions.text: How is the cycling space separated from walking or motor traffic?

options.text: Separate from people walking, at the same level
Different level or kerb from people walking

questions.text: Is the cycling infrastructure one-way or two-way?
What surface does the cycling infrastructure have?
How many places are there where motor vehicles cross or enter the cycling space?
Who else commonly uses the cycling space?
How often do other vehicles or people occupy the cycling space?
How fast does motor traffic feel on this street?
What makes things difficult with traffic here?
questions.help: Side access means driveways, garage entrances or side streets where vehicles enter or leave the street.

options.text: Cars or motorcycles do not stop at the zebra crossing
Vehicles go through the red light
Bicycles, e-scooters or motorcycles on the sidewalk
The cycle path cuts across the sidewalk: bicycles and pedestrians cross paths

questions.text: How steep is the climb on this stretch?

options.text: Very steep climb, you need to stop

questions.text: What problems affect the walking surface?
questions.help: A side slope is when the walking surface tilts sideways, across the direction of walking.

options.text: No curb ramp to get on or off the sidewalk

questions.text: How often do surface problems slow you down or make you change path while walking?
What obstacles reduce the walking space?

options.text: Bicycles, e-scooters, or motorcycles parked on the sidewalk
Trees, poles, signs, or utility boxes

questions.text: How often do obstacles block or reduce your space while walking?
How often does this segment feel too crowded?
How often do motor vehicles pass too close while you are walking?
What problems make riding a bicycle or e-scooter less comfortable here?
How often do surface problems slow you down or make you change path on a bicycle or e-scooter?
What obstacles make it difficult to ride a bicycle or e-scooter here?

options.text: E-scooters, bicycles or motorcycles parked where I ride
Trees, poles, signs, or utility boxes
Public transport stop or people waiting

questions.text: How often do obstacles block or reduce your space on a bicycle or e-scooter?
How often do motor vehicles pass too close while you ride a bicycle or e-scooter?

sections.title: Improve this street segment
sections.description: Tell us whether improving this segment should be a priority.

questions.text: Should a continuous walking space be added here?
questions.help: A continuous walking space is a sidewalk or path without gaps along the whole stretch.

questions.text: Should a continuous cycle lane or path be added here?
questions.help: A continuous cycle lane or path runs along the whole stretch without gaps.

questions.text: How urgent is it to improve this street segment?
What would improve this street segment most?
questions.help: A curb ramp is a short slope that connects the sidewalk to the road.

options.text: Add a sidewalk or make it continuous
Add an alternative to stairs (ramp or elevator)
Add benches or places to sit

questions.text: Anything else you want to add?
questions.help: Please do not write names or other personal data.

fr.#Street section with a magnifying glass: Tronçon de rue avec une loupe
fr.#Select walking, cycling, or both. Quest: Sélectionnez la marche, le vélo ou les deux. Les questions s’adapteront à votre sélection.
fr.#How do you move through this place? You: Comment vous déplacez-vous dans ce lieu ? Vous pouvez choisir les deux réponses.
fr.#Person walking or rolling (also with a: Personne à pied (y compris avec une poussette, une canne, un déambulateur ou un fauteuil roulant)

fr.#Which of these situations apply to your: Lesquelles de ces situations s'appliquent à votre déplacement d'aujourd'hui ?
fr.#Going to or from a bus, tram or metro s: Je vais à un arrêt de bus, de tram ou de métro, ou j'en reviens
fr.#Going to or from a parked car: Je vais à une voiture garée ou j'en reviens
fr.#Going to or from bicycle parking: Je vais à un stationnement vélo ou j'en reviens
fr.#Accompanying a child (for example to sc: J'accompagne un enfant (par exemple à l'école)
fr.#Using a wheelchair, walker, cane or oth: J'utilise un fauteuil roulant, un déambulateur, une canne ou une autre aide à la mobilité
fr.#How often do you go along this street s: À quelle fréquence parcourez-vous ce tronçon de rue ?
fr.#I avoid it or have stopped using it: Je l'évite ou j'ai cessé de l'utiliser
fr.#Answer these first. Then you can finish: Répondez d’abord à ces questions. Ensuite, vous pouvez terminer ou ajouter des détails facultatifs.
fr.#Is there a place for people to walk alo: Y a-t-il un espace où les personnes peuvent marcher le long de cette rue ?
fr.#No walking space: people walk among the: Aucun espace pour marcher : on marche au milieu des voitures
fr.#Only an edge of the road, without a sid: Seulement un bord de route, sans trottoir
fr.#Sidewalk, but it stops or is only on on: Trottoir, mais il s'interrompt ou n'existe que d'un côté
fr.#Walking space marked on the ground, at: Espace piéton marqué au sol, au même niveau que la chaussée
fr.#Path shared by people walking and cycli: Chemin partagé entre piétons et cyclistes
fr.#Stairway or path with steps (stairways: Escalier ou chemin avec des marches (les escaliers s’évaluent ici)
fr.#Is there a space for cycling on this st: Y a-t-il un espace pour les vélos dans cette rue ?
fr.#A school street is a street next to a s: Une rue scolaire est une rue près d’une école, fermée aux véhicules motorisés à l’arrivée et au départ des enfants.
fr.#No space for bicycles: people cycle in: Aucun espace pour les vélos : on roule dans la circulation normale
fr.#No space for bicycles, but the limit is: Aucun espace pour les vélos, mais la vitesse est limitée à 30 km/h ou c’est une rue scolaire
fr.#Cycle lane or path, but it stops: Bande ou piste cyclable, mais elle s'interrompt
fr.#Which best describes using this street: Quelle phrase décrit le mieux l’utilisation de ce tronçon à pied ?
fr.#I need to be careful while passing: Je dois faire attention en passant
fr.#It takes a lot of effort or attention: Cela me demande beaucoup d'effort ou d'attention
fr.#I cannot get through (for example with: Je ne peux pas passer (par exemple avec un fauteuil roulant ou une poussette)
fr.#Because of traffic (cars, motorcycles,: À cause de la circulation (voitures, motos, vélos), à quel point vous semble-t-il risqué de parcourir ce tronçon de rue à pied ?
fr.#Which best describes using this street: Quelle phrase décrit le mieux l’utilisation de ce tronçon à vélo ou en trottinette électrique ?
fr.#I cannot get through by bicycle or e-sc: Je ne peux pas passer à vélo ou en trottinette électrique
fr.#Because of traffic, how risky does it f: À cause de la circulation, à quel point vous semble-t-il risqué d’emprunter ce tronçon à vélo ou en trottinette électrique ?
fr.#How safe from harassment or assault do: Dans quelle mesure vous sentez-vous ici à l'abri du harcèlement ou des agressions, y compris le soir ?
fr.#Harassment means unwanted comments, ges: Le harcèlement désigne des commentaires, gestes ou contacts non désirés. Cette question porte sur votre ressenti, pas sur la circulation.
fr.#Neither safe nor unsafe: Ni en sécurité ni en insécurité
fr.#I do not go there in the evening: Je n'y passe pas le soir
fr.#Would you like to add more details? The: Souhaitez-vous ajouter d’autres détails ? Il y a environ 10 à 20 questions facultatives pour un mode de déplacement, et jusqu’à environ 30 si vous avez choisi les deux (environ 4 à 10 minutes).
fr.#Look at the place. Answer only what you: Observez le lieu. Répondez uniquement à ce que vous pouvez voir.
fr.#How wide is the space for walking?: Quelle est la largeur de l'espace pour marcher ?
fr.#Only one person can just about pass: Une seule personne passe tout juste

fr.#Paint or road markings only: Peinture ou marquages au sol uniquement
fr.#Tactile paving is a ridged or dotted gr: Les bandes podotactiles sont des surfaces au sol à stries ou à plots que les personnes aveugles ou malvoyantes peuvent sentir avec leur canne ou leurs pieds.
fr.#Tactile paving for blind or visually im: Bande d’éveil à la vigilance pour les personnes aveugles ou malvoyantes
fr.#Are there steps or stairs along this pa: Y a-t-il des marches ou des escaliers sur ce chemin ?
